items.headline: Protecting existing Amazon forests beats restoration for saving wildlife and carbon, study finds
items.summary: A large study tracking more than three million hectares of Brazilian Amazon rainforest over a decade found that preventing logging and wildfires in standing forests protects more wildlife than planting new trees, and nearly matches restoration for storing carbon, at a lower cost. Restoration still matters where forest has already been cleared, but the research shows guarding what remains often delivers the biggest return per dollar spent.
items.why_it_matters: It gives conservation groups and governments a clearer, more cost-effective playbook for protecting the Amazon's biodiversity and climate value with limited funding.
